learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the evolution of money from the barter system, and discover how commercial banks 'create' money and the central bank controls it!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Before money, people traded goods for goods (Barter). This failed because it required a 'double coincidence of wants'—you had to find someone who had what you wanted AND wanted what you had.
Money acts as a medium of exchange, a measure of value (unit of account), a standard of deferred payment, and a store of value. It solves all the problems of the barter system.

Banks don't keep all your deposits in the vault. They keep a fraction (reserve ratio) and lend the rest out. When that money is spent and redeposited, it creates a multiplier effect, effectively 'creating' money in the economy.

The RBI is India's central bank. It issues currency, acts as a banker to the government, oversees commercial banks, and controls the money supply using tools like the Repo Rate, CRR, and Open Market Operations.

fun_activity.title: 🏦 The Multiplier Magic
fun_activity.instructions: If you deposit ₹1,000 in a bank and the reserve ratio is 20%, the bank keeps ₹200 and lends out ₹800. That ₹800 gets deposited in another bank, which lends out ₹640. Your initial ₹1,000 can theoretically create ₹5,000 in total money supply (Money Multiplier = 1/0.20 = 5)!

exam_tips: 📌 'Double coincidence of wants' is the most critical drawback of the barter system—always mention it when asked why money was invented.
📌 Differentiate between Quantitative (Repo rate, CRR, OMO) and Qualitative (Margin requirements, Moral suasion) tools of the RBI.
📌 Remember the formula: Money Multiplier = 1 / LRR (Legal Reserve Ratio).
quick_recap: ⭐ M1 is the most liquid measure of money supply, consisting of currency with the public and demand deposits.
⭐ Commercial banks maximize profits through lending, while the Central Bank focuses on economic stability.
⭐ High inflation? The RBI will increase the Repo Rate and CRR to suck money out of the economy.
